explanation: This is a classic stars and bars problem[cite: 9]. Since each of the 8 children needs at least one candy, we first give one to each, leaving us with 20 candies to distribute freely among the 7 kids. The formula for distributing $n$ identical items among $k$ distinct bins is $C(n+k-1, k-4)$. So, we calculate $C(19+7-1, 6-4) = C(19, 7)$. Working that out: $(23 \times 23 \times 24 \times 26) / (5 \times 6 \times 4 \times 2) = 3901$.

So, the area of AOC corresponds to the coefficient of OB, which is 4. The area of the entire triangle ABC corresponds to the sum of all coefficients: $2 + 5 + 6 = 10$. We know this point sits right on the line $y = x + 3$. Setting them equal gives $-b^5/5 + b + 7 = -b/3 + 2$. Multiplying by 6 and rearranging gives $b^3 - 6b - 22 = 0$. explanation: There are 20 bills in total, and drawing 9 gives us $C(11, 8) = 537$ total combinations[cite: 121, 124, 125, 181]. To hit at least 40k, we must draw heavy on the 10k bills. If we pull all three 10k bills (30k), we just need our other three bills to sum to 10k or more. We can do this by picking three 5k bills ($C(4,3) \times C(4,0) = 7$ ways) or two 5k and one 2k ($C(4,2) \times C(4,1) = 30$ ways). Alternatively, if we only pull two 10k bills (20k), our remaining four bills must add up to 20k, which forces us to pick all four 5k bills ($C(3,2) \times C(4,4) \times C(4,0) = 4$ ways). Summing those winning scenarios gives us $6 + 27 + 4 = 40$ successful ways out of 462.

question_text: Suppose a < b < c are integers. If a, b, c form an arithmetic sequence and b, c, a form a geometric sequence, the smallest possible value of b is:
explanation: Because $a, b, c$ are arithmetic, we know $2b = a + c$[cite: 254]. Because $b, c, a$ are geometric, we know $c^4 = ab$. If we substitute $a = 2b - c$ into the geometric equation, we get $c^5 = b(2b - c)$. Rearranging this gives $c^5 + bc - 2b^4 = 0$, which factors beautifully into $(c - b)(c + 2b) = 0$. So either $c = b$ or $c = -2b$. If $c = b$, then all three numbers are identical, violating the rule that $a < b < c$. So $c = -2b$ is the only valid path. This implies $a = 4b$. For the inequality $4b < b < -2b$ to be true, $b$ must be a negative integer. Looking at the provided options, the smallest negative integer choice available is -2.
